correctness.rationale: The signed recurrence is derived by conditioning on the last independent vertex, with boundary conventions explicit. Over F2 its companion matrix has seventh power I, yielding exhaustive residue-by-residue parity obstructions. The seven-letter cancellation w_{m+7}=-t_3 t_5 w_m is a short direct recurrence identity under t_6=-t_5,t_7=-1; the 32 choices concatenate without restriction. Exact base signs prove zero existence and the sharp positive lower bounds, and 1,3,6 base zero counts multiplied by 32^k yield distinct null frequencies. Normalized character diagonalization, not a numerical extrapolation, gives exact ℓ2 inverse and pseudoinverse norms. Independent exact integer script agrees for all frequencies through n=16 and verifies the extension and parity structure.

originality.rationale: The 2012 and 2014 path-power papers prove unsigned counts, the independent-set recurrence and Hasse-diagram counts, not unit-sign Walsh zero existence or exact nonzero gaps. The 2003 multivariate independent-set polynomial framework gives the evaluation language and a general vertex-deletion recurrence, but its polydisc nonvanishing criteria do not imply the path-square unit-sign classification. A published result on graph-independent-set restricted Fourier matrices has a different operator and does not cover full-group convolution. Distinct previously indexed results for ordinary-path maximal independent sets and the Fibonacci-cube XOR-difference function do not imply the present h=2 independent-set multiplier claim. The specific 32-way seven-block cancellation mechanism and all-length sharp least positive multiplier were not located by the actual targeted searches; historical priority is not absolutely established.
residual_risks: Unindexed or older literature may express the same period-seven result as a multivariate independence-polynomial sign-vertex zero theorem.

value.rationale: The complete Fourier invertibility classification, exact sharp positive spectral gap, and explicit exponential kernel-dimension lower bounds are canonical invariants of the indicator of all independent sets in the square of a path. They determine whether convolution can reconstruct arbitrary data and exactly how badly its inverse behaves in ℓ2. The seven-sign identity gives a nontrivial structural mechanism behind cancellations, not simply a parity table or a narrow arbitrary finite slice; the objects were independently motivated in pre-2016 generalized Fibonacci-cube literature.
